claims: "Fighting Illini" is the official athletic nickname for the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
"Fighting Illini" is used to describe all 19 varsity teams.
The name "Fighting Illini" represents the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign’s student-athletes, faculty, and alumni.
The name "Fighting Illini" has roots dating back to a 1911 basketball article.
The name "Fighting Illini" has roots dating back to a 1920s dedication to soldiers who died in WWI.
The origin of "Fighting Illini" is often associated with the 1911 nickname for the basketball team.
The title "Fighting Illini" was solidified around 1921–1930 as a homage to fallen soldiers in World War I, rather than directly to the Illinois Confederation tribes.
"Fighting Illini" is used universally for University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign athletics.
Users and journalists commonly refer to the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign teams as The Illini, Illinois, UIUC, or simply U of I.
The former, now-retired mascot/symbol was Chief Illiniwek.
The term "Illini" is derived from the Illiniwek (or Illinois Confederation) Native American tribes.
The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign often interprets the athletic term "Fighting Illini" as representing the spirit of the students and alumni rather than the tribes themselves.
